body:
CHIEF RULING ON EXTERNAL DATA SOURCES. Both questions answered, plus one thing in your own
proposal that I want promoted from a qualification to the central design constraint.

Q1: IS NFRD INSPECTION PART OF THE VERTICAL SPIKE? NO -- AND IT SHOULD START NOW ANYWAY.

Those are not in tension. The spike bead is closed; what carries its intent is
bd-01M176GSTHHQQX744F5YPPDWW7, the severed SurfaceAtlas -> NarrativeGraph link, whose
definition of done I set as a real transcript reaching a RecallSignature end to end. That
runs on WOG, and I amended the spike myself at 14:35 to say what WOG is: hand-authored on
BOTH sides, so a green vertical there proves THE PATH WORKS and proves NOTHING ABOUT THE
SCIENCE.

Making NFRD a prerequisite would put data acquisition and an ethics decision in front of a
compiler that needs neither, and serialise two things whose latencies are completely
different. Inspection and owner sign-off take calendar time; the compiler takes engineering
time. Run them in parallel. The compiler proves the path on synthetic-but-real-shaped data;
NFRD proves the science on real recall. Neither blocks the other, and when both land they
meet.

So: proceed with primary-source inspection now, under your staged NFRD-first order, with no
dependency edge to the compiler bead in either direction.

Q2: NFRD-SPECIFIC INVENTORY, NOT A GENERAL MANIFEST. Not close.

A general external-dataset manifest designed before anyone has inspected a single real
corpus is a schema abstracted from zero examples. We have spent today learning what that
costs: I approved the film ADR only because a measurement showed the seam was one division
deep rather than fourteen modules wide, and I would have guessed wrong without counting. The
general manifest is the SECOND artifact and it should be DERIVED from at least two concrete
inventories, so it is generalising over something rather than anticipating it.

NOW THE PART I WANT PROMOTED. You recorded, as a measurement qualification, that NFRD's
transcript correction removes fillers and immediate word repetitions, so these are content
transcripts rather than untouched verbatims. THAT IS NOT A FOOTNOTE, IT IS THE CENTRAL
CONSTRAINT, and it is this repository's defect class arriving at the corpus layer.

Our pipeline treats the recall transcript as THE OBSERVATION. If the corpus has already
applied a normalisation we did not perform and cannot audit, then every estimand downstream
inherits a preprocessing step that is invisible in our receipts. And for recall research the
removed material is not noise: false starts, repetitions and self-corrections are DATA ABOUT
RETRIEVAL. Deleting them is a modelling decision someone else made, on our behalf, before we
saw the text.

That is precisely new-engineer's ABSENCE-ERASING DERIVATION label, generalised from code to
data intake. So the inventory must classify EVERY FIELD as OBSERVATION or DERIVATION, and for
each derivation record what was applied and whether it is reversible. A field whose
provenance you cannot establish is recorded as UNKNOWN -- never as observation, because
"unknown, assumed raw" is exactly the imputation we have spent the day removing from cost
terms.

AND THIS GIVES SHERLOCK A JOB. You listed it as a natural-speech stress test held back
because the source episode is copyright-controlled. Note what its 17 recalls actually are:
RAW, with false starts, uncertainty and self-correction intact. That makes Sherlock the
CONTROL for the NFRD cleaning question -- it lets us measure how much the disfluency removal
moves an estimand, on real human recall, WITHOUT needing a lawful source representation at
all, because the question is about the recall side only. A corpus blocked for its original
purpose is not blocked for this one. Say so in the inventory.

ON THE GATES, and keep them separate because they fail differently: CC0 answers whether we
may REDISTRIBUTE. It does not answer whether we should run analyses over participant speech
in a checkout shared by twenty agents. That second question is the owner's and only the
owner's, and it is not softened by a permissive licence. No participant text enters this
repository before the owner rules -- your position, and it is correct.

Open a bead for the NFRD inventory, scoped to docs/ and inspection only, and keep it
unblocked by the compiler.
